candidates.title: Guided snowmobile day on groomed Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean trails
candidates.summary: Rental sleds with a guide on the regional groomed network out of Saguenay. This suits the mixed party because the two novices get a briefing and ride on maintained trail, and you can choose shorter loops well within the 180 km range. Destination, ages and access needs were not answered, so I could not check whether this fits everyone. A trail permit is usually needed, and I have not confirmed whether the rental includes it.

candidates.title: Beginner snowmobile orientation session
candidates.summary: A short instruction session for the two first-time riders before any longer trail day. It covers controls, trail signage and safe following distance on groomed routes. I do not know of a specific provider, how long a session runs or what it costs, so those are left unknown.

candidates.summary: Winter fishing cabins out on the frozen fjord at La Baie, and you can reach the area by sled on short groomed segments. It makes a lower-effort break between riding days. Ice conditions and the open period vary from year to year and I have not checked them; this is not clearance to go out on the ice.

candidatesAccepted.title: Trail conditions check: Québec snowmobile federation trail map
candidatesAccepted.summary: Groomed-trail status around Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean changes daily in late January and February. The authoritative source is the Fédération des clubs de motoneigistes du Québec (FCMQ) interactive trail map and the local club bulletins. Use these, not this note, to judge whether a loop is open. A trail access pass (droit d'accès) is required on FCMQ trails; rental outfits often include it, so confirm with them. The destination was not answered, so no specific loop is assessed here.

candidatesAccepted.title: Cold-weather riding kit for first-timers
candidatesAccepted.summary: Saguenay in late January can run well below −25 °C with wind chill on the machine. Two riders have never ridden, so check that the rental includes or rents insulated one-piece suits, boots, mitts, a full-face modular helmet with breath box or heated visor, and a balaclava. Ask about hand and thumb warmers. For forecasts and extreme-cold warnings, Environment and Climate Change Canada is the authority. Ages and access needs were not answered and are not accounted for.

candidatesAccepted.title: Guided intro and short groomed loop for novices
candidatesAccepted.summary: A guided half-day on groomed trail lets the two new riders learn throttle, braking and leaning before longer legs. This fits the group's stated preference for fewer kilometres on groomed trail. Guides know current trail and lake-ice status, but local clubs and the outfitter remain the authority. Do not treat this note as clearance; never cross lake or river ice unless it is a marked, open trail.

candidatesAccepted.title: Fuel and range planning on the trail network
candidatesAccepted.summary: The stated range between stops is 180 km. Cold and novice riding raise fuel use, so plan fuel at trailside relais well inside that range and confirm their winter opening with the relais or the club. Simple lodging at trailside relais suits the 'simple' night tolerance. Opening dates and prices are unverified, and peak February weekends book up.

candidatesAccepted.title: Snowmobile trail permit (droit d'accès) for Québec federated trails
candidatesAccepted.summary: Riding the FCMQ groomed trail network requires a valid trail access right per machine; rental outfitters around Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean often include it in the rental, so confirm whether yours does before buying separately. Destination is not answered, so the trail region could not be checked.

candidatesAccepted.summary: Québec requires snowmobile drivers on public trails to meet age rules and carry civil liability insurance; confirm the rental contract's liability coverage, damage deductible and whether a valid driver's licence is needed to cross roads. candidatesAccepted.summary: Cell coverage drops between villages on the Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean and Monts-Valin trails; renting a satellite messenger or PLB and downloading the iMotoneige trail app offline gives a fallback for a 180 km range.
